input: *Nicco turns on his stool toward the loud man.* Friend, she's working as fast as she can. Maybe give her a moment.
draft:
Dell Harrow's heavy-lidded gaze swung toward Nicco. His mouth worked once before the words came, slow and sour. "Friend," he repeated, dragging the word out like it tasted wrong. "I don't know you, and you don't know me, so don't tell me when I've had enough." He jabbed a finger in Jessa's direction without looking at her. "She knows my money's good."

Jessa Rook didn't raise her voice. She set the rag she'd been holding down on the counter, and her hand came to rest beside it — not reaching for anything, just resting. "Dell. Your money's always good. That's not what this is about." Her tone carried the particular steadiness of someone who has said a version of this sentence before. "You're loud, it's late, and you're making the man next to you uncomfortable. Finish the one you've got."

Dell's jaw tightened. He looked from Jessa to Nicco and back again, shoulders bunched under the salt-stained coat. For a moment the common room was quieter than it had any right to be with people in it. Then he pulled his mug closer and turned back to his own table, muttering something into the rim of it that didn't carry.

Jessa picked the rag up again. Her eyes stayed on Dell a beat longer before she turned back along the counter.
